findings.title: New preview feature ROLLING_UPDATES is not added to the documented feature list
findings.body: This PR introduces a new preview feature, ROLLING_UPDATES (key 'rolling-updates'), but the server documentation page that enumerates supported/preview/experimental features (docs/guides/server/features.adoc, the 'Enabling and disabling features' guide) is not updated. Users looking up what `--features=rolling-updates` enables, or which preview features exist, will find no mention of it, even though other guides in this same PR instruct users to enable it. The feature table should be updated in the same change that adds the enum entry.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is repurposed from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED code takes the value 4. The documentation has always stated 3 means 'recreate required', so the code change fixes an inconsistency; however, any automation written against the previously shipped binary observed exit code 4 for 'recreate required'. After this change, such a script that checks `exit == 4` will instead see it when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, and could wrongly conclude a recreate (downtime) upgrade is required, or vice versa miss a genuine recreate signal now delivered as 3. Since the guide explicitly tells users to build automation on the exit codes, a release note or version-aware handling should accompany this repurposing.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path only tested for 'metadata' and without asserting the new exit code 4
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the `metadata` subcommand and only asserts the error message text. The documentation added in this PR promises a specific exit code 4 ('The feature rolling-updates is disabled') and the same gate is implemented in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata, but neither the exit code nor the `check` subcommand's disabled path is verified. If the gate is accidentally removed, the exit code changes, or the check command crashes (e.g., NPE from Profile not being initialized) instead of exiting 4, no test would catch it. The test should assert exitCode() == 4 and cover `check` as well.
